current.text: He had wrist surgery after the playoffs. He is expected to be ready for opening night.
He played two extra months in the Knicks' championship run and was Finals MVP.
Experts worry about a Finals hangover. He may start slow, lose some production to fatigue and have his minutes protected.
The Knicks are expected to be careful with their starters over the first 30 or so games. That means trimmed minutes and more rest on back-to-backs.
He is the projected starting guard next to Bridges, Hart, Anunoby and Towns.
He is projected at about 31 percent usage and 35 minutes.
The Knicks are projected to win about 50 to 54 games.

Experts value him as a fourth-round player in category leagues, around picks 39 to 48. Early round 3 is too soon, and his Yahoo ADP in the 20s is too high. One expert gives a best case of 22nd and a worst case of 91st.
In a mock auction, Josh valued him at about 18 USD and bid up to 19 USD. He went for 20 USD.

durable.text: He is a high-usage scorer. Points are his standout category.
His free throw shooting is good.
He barely rebounds and gets few steals. His blocks are very poor, even for a guard.
Experts disagree on his field goal percentage. Some call it good or solid, one calls it below average. Projections put his FG% impact near the pool average.
Experts call his assists average to decent.
He is worth much more in points leagues than in category leagues. Points-based rankings overrate him for us.

note: The market prices Brunson as a top-30 player: Yahoo average cost 32.6 USD, ESPN 42.9 USD, and 31 USD in our league last season. The experts see a fourth-round category player (picks 39 to 48) and valued him at 18 to 20 USD in a mock auction, so let someone else pay 30 USD or more. He fits builds that want points, FT% and threes from a guard, and suits punt BLK. Early in the season, check his minutes and rest days under the Knicks' careful plan for the first 30 or so games, and check his wrist after surgery.
